course_profile.one_sentence_summary: A foundational programming course teaching the core constructs, memory management, and procedural paradigms of the C programming language.
course_profile.short_summary: This course is the first part of a foundational programming sequence for software engineering students. It focuses on the C programming language, covering essential syntax, control structures, pointers, dynamic memory allocation, functions, user-defined structures, and file I/O operations. Through lectures and computer practicums, students learn to design algorithms, draw flowcharts, and implement efficient procedural code.

theoretical_understanding: Understand variable lifecycles and memory classes (automatic, static, external, register).
Grasp the difference between pass-by-value and pass-by-reference in function calls.
Understand how data is stored and manipulated at the memory address level using pointers.
practical_implementation: Write, compile, and execute C programs implementing linear and iterative algorithms.
Manage memory dynamically during program execution for single and multidimensional arrays.
Read from and write to standard text and binary files utilizing both stream-based and low-level I/O.
analysis_validation: Analyze mathematical models to formulate corresponding algorithmic workflows.
Debug and validate basic programmatic code during computer practicums.
architecture_design: Decompose complex tasks into modular, reusable functional blocks using C functions.
Design custom data structures using unions and structs.

implementation_tasks: File processing using varying I/O levels
engineering_practices: Documentation of logic via flowcharts and reports

curricular_relations.reason: Mastery of C syntax and concepts is required before effectively learning pointer operations.
Pointers are the foundational prerequisite mechanism used in C to interact with dynamically allocated memory blocks.
The ability to conceptualize algorithms directly translates into writing logical structures in C code.

what_student_can_understand: How high-level procedural logic translates to hardware manipulation via memory addresses and pointers.
The lifecycle of variables and programmatic memory classes.
what_student_can_build: Command-line software utilities that execute sorting, manipulation, and math routines.
Programs capable of long-term data processing via file stream manipulation.
what_student_can_apply: Modularization and safe memory handling practices.
